success_patterns: A bare quoted line from a poem or song, with no 'this' pointer, was answered with its author (Joyce Kilmer). The agent matched the repeated line across many passages and named the creator.

A translation clue ('translates to this in English') was answered with the English gloss the passages print in parentheses next to the foreign title ('My Crazy Life'). The agent ignored the self-introduction aside '(Hi, I'm Pam Tillis)' and the quotation marks.

A pun on a quoted word ('large "steak"' plus 'Marquess of this') was resolved by finding the food or idiom the word echoes (Salisbury steak). The agent answered with the bare name the passages pair with that word and left off 'Marquess of' and 'Steak'.

For 'this <country/state/crop>' clues, the agent answered with the container or category instance that recurs across many passages next to the clue's distinctive anchor (Judeo-Galilean Highlands -> Israel; Andrew Johnson -> Tennessee; Bharat Ratna -> India). It gave the bare form with no head noun and used the plural for the crop (Bananas).

patch.reasoning: Most successes were already covered by the existing rules on the referent, bare-answer formatting and quoted-word puns. Two patterns are not stated explicitly and recurred. First, a bare quotation clue with no 'this' pointer asks for its author or source. Second, a translation clue asks for the gloss the passages give. Both are short, general additions. Earlier rejected patches were long and added many narrow rules, so only two compact edits are proposed here.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a quoted line of a poem, song, speech or famous quotation ('"I think that I shall never see a poem lovely as a tree"') asks for its AUTHOR or creator ('Joyce Kilmer'), not the poem title, unless the clue says 'this poem/song'. The passages repeat the line next to the creator's name.
- Translation clues ('"Mi Vida Loca" translates to this in English', 'in English, this is...'): the passages print the English gloss in parentheses or beside the foreign title ('Mi Vida Loca (My Crazy Life)'). Copy that gloss without quotation marks. Ignore speaker intros or asides such as '(Hi, I'm Pam Tillis)'.

edits.target: Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content: - Pun clues: a quoted homophone ('a large "steak" in British politics', 'The Marquess of this') points to a compound the passages contain ('Salisbury steak'). Answer with the bare name that pairs with the pun word ('Salisbury'), not the pun word itself, the title ('Marquess of') or the full compound.
